analysis_trace.content: NCT06968221 is a Phase 3 randomized trial comparing Cingular Bovine Pericardium Anastomosis Reinforcement Membrane (bioabsorbable staple line reinforcement) versus standard non-reinforced stapling in stomach, colorectal, and lung anastomoses for Stage III rectal and lung cancer patients. Primary completion expected September 2025. Status: RECRUITING.

Adults 18-75 years undergoing stapled stomach, colorectal, or lung anastomosis. Exclusions: significant hypotension, cardiac events, collagen vascular disease, coagulopathy, renal/hepatic dysfunction, uncontrolled intra-abdominal infection. Mixed cancer population (rectal Stage III, lung Stage III). Estimated enrollment 172 subjects.

Bovine pericardium ECM reinforcement patch aims to strengthen staple line, enhance vascular sealing, and reduce bleeding/leakage. Mechanism: compression effect on cross-cut tissue improving hemostasis; physical reinforcement of anastomotic site during healing.

Primary-0: Proportion with hemorrhage through 10 min post-procedure (immediate hemostasis endpoint). Secondary-0: Proportion with clinical/radiologic anastomotic leak through 1-3 months post-procedure (healing/integrity endpoint). Both are binary proportion endpoints comparing reinforced vs standard.

Retrieved evidence: (1) Frontiers Bioeng Biotechnol 2023 review on staple line reinforcement materials showing SIS and bovine pericardium patches reduce bleeding and leakage rates; (2) Frontiers Surgery 2024 review reporting colorectal AL rates 2.8%-30% depending on definition and site; (3) PMC11097957 confirms AL rates vary by anastomotic location; (4) Gore Medical literature showing staple line reinforcement reduces intraoperative bleeding. No direct Phase 3 results for Cingular product available pre-cutoff.

Evidence on staple line reinforcement efficacy: indirect_direction for both endpoints - supports directional benefit but not precise numeric estimate. Bovine pericardium specifically: mechanism_background - biocompatible ECM with hemostatic properties. Published AL rates: indirect_direction - establishes baseline range for control arm. No direct_numeric evidence for Cingular in this exact population.

Hemorrhage at 10 min: Based on mechanism (compression hemostasis) and class evidence, reinforcement expected to reduce immediate bleeding. Typical intraoperative staple line bleeding rates without reinforcement 5-15%; with reinforcement expected reduction to 2-8%. Predicted absolute risk reduction ~5-7 percentage points. Confidence moderate given indirect evidence.

Anastomotic leak 1-3 months: Class evidence mixed - some RCTs show no significant leak reduction with reinforcement (e.g., Dis Colon Rectum 2014: >5cm from anal verge no leak benefit). However, bovine pericardium may benefit higher-risk anastomoses. Baseline leak rate for colorectal ~6-12% (low anterior), 1-3% (colocolonic). Predicted modest reduction or equivalence. Lower confidence given heterogeneity in leak definitions and anastomotic sites.

Bovine pericardium ECM generally well-tolerated. Potential risks: foreign body reaction, infection, delayed degradation. Trial exclusions limit high-risk patients. No specific safety signals identified in retrieved evidence.

(1) Mixed anastomotic sites (stomach, colorectal, lung) with different baseline leak/bleed rates may dilute treatment effect; (2) Stage III cancer patients may have higher complication risk; (3) 10-minute hemorrhage endpoint may miss delayed bleeding; (4) 1-3 month leak window may miss late leaks.

Indirect evidence supports hemostasis benefit (primary-0) more consistently than leak reduction (secondary-0). Mechanistic rationale stronger for immediate bleeding control than for long-term anastomotic healing. Historical RCTs of synthetic reinforcement showed leak benefit mainly in high-risk/distal anastomoses.

No direct Phase 3 results for Cingular product; no published data on 10-minute hemorrhage endpoint specifically; limited data on bovine pericardium in lung anastomoses; anastomotic leak definition variability limits cross-study comparison.
